sentences.text:
The Food Inspector, Circleii, vs Laxminivas Sharma on 15
October, 2024
 The Honourable Sri Justice K.Surender
 Criminal Appeal No.231 Of 2013
Judgment:

entities.text: Food Inspector, Circleii, vs Laxminivas Sharma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
1. The Food Inspector has filed the present appeal represented by the Public Prosecutor, questioning the acquittal of the respondent/accused for the offence under Sections 7(i) and 2(ia)(m), 16 (1)(a)(i)
of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and Rules 50 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act & Rules 1955.

entities.text: Prevention of Food Adulteration Act & Rules 1955
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
2. Heard learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the appellant, learned counsel for the respondents and perused the entire material on record.
3.

Briefly, the case of the Food Inspector/PW.1 is that on 18.09.1999 he along with others went to the premises of M/s Agarwal Industries Limited for the purpose of inspection and found 78 boxes of Gold Mohar Vanaspati of 15 liters and sealed pouches of 500 ml of Gold Mohar Vanaspati.
PW.1 secured the presence of two independent witnesses and conducted the search.
He purchased three packets of oil and made them as samples.
One of the sample was sent to the public analyst for the purpose of opinion.
In the opinion, the public analyst stated that the sample does not conform to the standards of Red Units in respect of 'Baudouin's Test' and accordingly it was adulterated.

4. The learned Magistrate relying on the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in State Vs. Mahavir Prashad1 held that baudouin's test is not sure test to find the presence of Seasame Oil in Vanaspati.
Further, the learned trial Judge found that since nutritive value of the oil will not be affected, it cannot be said that the purity would fall below the prescribed standard.
The learned Magistrate further found that there was no counter argument in respect of the said judgment.
Further, the trial Court found that the sampling done was not in 1972 FAC 603 accordance with law since the sealed packets were cut open and samples were drawn.

5. In cases of acquittal, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ravi Sharma v. State (Government of NCT of Delhi) and another2, held that while dealing with an appeal against acquittal, the appellate court has to consider whether the trial Court's view can be termed as a possible one, particularly when evidence on record has been analyzed.

entities.text: Ravi Sharma v. State (Government of NCT of Delhi)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The reason is that an order of acquittal adds up to the presumption of innocence in favour of the accused.
Thus, the appellate court has to be relatively slow in reversing the order of the trial court rendering acquittal.

6. In Ghurey Lal v. State of Uttar Pradesh3 the Hon'ble Supreme Court after referring to several Judgments regarding the settled principles of law and the (2022) 8 Supreme Court Cases 536 (2008) 10 Supreme Court Cases 450 powers of appellate Court in reversing the order of acquittal,
held at para 70, as follows:

1 "70. In the light of the above, the High Court and other appellate Courts should follow the well-settled principles crystallized by number of Judgments if it is going to overrule or otherwise disturb the trial court's acquittal:
1.

entities.text: Ghurey Lal v. State of Uttar Pradesh3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: (2022) 8 Supreme Court Cases 536 (2008) 10 Supreme Court Cases 450
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Food Inspector, Circleii, vs Laxminivas Sharma
entities.label: PETITIONER

sentences.text: The appellate court may only overrule or otherwise disturb the trial court's acquittal if it has "very substantial and compelling reasons" for doing so.
A number of instances arise in which the appellate court would have "very substantial and compelling reasons" to discard the trial court's decision.
If two reasonable views can be reached__ one that leads to acquittal, the other to conviction __the High Courts/appellate courts must rule in favour of the accused."

7. Since the test that was conducted was not conclusive and it was not specifically mentioned as to the exact reason for certifying its adulteration, the learned Magistrate had not committed any error in acquitting the accused.
Further sealed packets have to be sent in the same form and cannot be cut and mixed to draw samples.
Hence, I do not find any reason to interfere with the judgement of the learned trial Court.
8. Accordingly, the appeal stands dismissed.
K.SURENDER, J Date: 15.10.2024 mmr
